description: Real backend authentication: register, login, and me endpoints with Bun.password hashing (argon2/bcrypt) and stateless JWT, plus a reusable auth guard that later protected routes use to resolve the authenticated user id. Nothing security-relevant is trusted from the client. Depends on FEAT-002 (users table) and FEAT-001 (Elysia app composition). This FEAT establishes the per-user isolation primitive that FEAT-005 relies on.
steps: Create c:\Users\PravallikaP\Documents\FDE capstone\online_bookstore\src\lib\auth.ts: read JWT secret from process.env.JWT_SECRET with a documented dev fallback constant (e.g. 'dev-only-insecure-secret-change-me'); export signToken(userId) and verifyToken(token) producing/validating a stateless JWT (HS256) with an expiry (e.g. 7d). Use Bun.password.hash / Bun.password.verify for password hashing (argon2id default). Export hashPassword/verifyPassword wrappers. Export an Elysia-compatible guard (a `derive`/`resolve` or `macro`) that reads the Authorization: Bearer header, verifies the JWT, loads the user from the DB, and exposes { userId, user } to handlers; if missing/invalid it throws a 401 with JSON { error: 'Unauthorized' }.

Create c:\Users\PravallikaP\Documents\FDE capstone\online_bookstore\src\api\auth.ts: an Elysia instance exposing POST /register (body validated with Elysia t.Object: email, password min length, name), POST /login (email, password), GET /me (protected by the auth guard). register: reject duplicate email with 409 { error }, hash the password, insert the user with gift_points default (e.g. 0 or a small welcome balance), create the user's cart row, return { token, user } (never return password_hash). login: look up by email, verifyPassword, on success return { token, user }, on failure 401 { error: 'Invalid credentials' }. me: return the current user (id, email, name, gift_points) from the guard. Validation failures return 400 with a consistent JSON error shape.
Mount auth routes in c:\Users\PravallikaP\Documents\FDE capstone\online_bookstore\src\api\index.ts via .use(authRoutes) so endpoints resolve under /api/auth/*.
Add GET /api/points (or fold the gift_points balance into /api/auth/me) returning the authenticated user's gift_points; keep whichever the frontend will call documented in findings.

Create c:\Users\PravallikaP\Documents\FDE capstone\online_bookstore\src\api\auth.test.ts using a temp DB: register a user (expect token + user, no password_hash), reject duplicate email (409), login with correct creds (token), reject wrong password (401), call /me without a token (401) and with the token (200 returns the user), and verify a tampered/garbage token is rejected (401).
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/auth/register creates a user with a Bun.password-hashed password and returns a JWT and the user object without password_hash; duplicate email returns 409.
POST /api/auth/login returns a valid JWT for correct credentials and 401 for wrong credentials.
GET /api/auth/me returns the authenticated user for a valid Bearer token and 401 without/with an invalid token.
The exported auth guard resolves userId from the JWT and is reusable by other route modules.
`bun test` passes the auth tests and `bunx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
verification: Run `bun test src/api/auth.test.ts` (and the full `bun test`) and confirm all auth tests pass.
Run `bunx tsc --noEmit` and confirm zero errors.

Boot the server background/bounded, then with Invoke-RestMethod: POST /api/auth/register, POST /api/auth/login to capture $token, GET /api/auth/me with header @{ Authorization = "Bearer $token" } (expect the user), and GET /api/auth/me with no header (expect 401 via Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing checking StatusCode). Stop the server afterward.
findings:
DONE. All 5 acceptance criteria met: register/login/me work, duplicate=409, wrong creds=401, missing/invalid/tampered token=401, bun test (17 pass incl. 12 auth) green, bunx tsc --noEmit clean, background-boot probe confirmed (register token+no password_hash+gift_points=0, login token, /me OK, /me no-auth=401).

=== AUTH GUARD REUSE PATTERN (FEAT-004/005/006 MUST follow this) ===
File: src/lib/auth.ts. The guard is a FACTORY, not a bare plugin:
  export const authGuard = (database: Database = sharedDb) => Elysia plugin
It uses `.resolve({ as: 'scoped' }, ...)` to expose { userId: number, user: UserRow } to downstream handlers, and `.error({ UNAUTHORIZED: UnauthorizedError })` + `.onError({ as: 'scoped' })` to map auth failure to 401 { error: 'Unauthorized' }. 'scoped' means the guard's resolve/error apply to the CURRENT plugin instance and routes defined AFTER `.use(authGuard(db))` on the SAME chain (and one level up), NOT globally — so protected routes must be chained after `.use(authGuard(database))`, and public routes (if any) defined BEFORE it. See src/api/auth.ts for the live example: /register and /login are defined before `.use(authGuard(database))`, then /me and /points after.

USAGE for a new protected route module (recommended shape — same factory+inject pattern used by auth.ts so tests can pass a temp DB):
  import { authGuard } from '../lib/auth';
  export const cartRoutes = (database = sharedDb) =>
    new Elysia({ prefix: '/cart' })
      .use(authGuard(database))
      .get('/', ({ userId, user }) => { /* userId is the authenticated user's id — scope ALL queries by it, never trust the client */ });
Mount in src/api/index.ts with `.use(cartRoutes())` (api has prefix '/api', module adds its own sub-prefix). Each protected module should call authGuard with its OWN db instance so the injected-DB test pattern works.

Helpers also exported from src/lib/auth.ts for reuse: hashPassword/verifyPassword (Bun.password argon2id), signToken(userId)/verifyToken(token) (stateless HS256, 7d exp, secret from process.env.JWT_SECRET with documented dev fallback DEV_JWT_SECRET='dev-only-insecure-secret-change-me'), findUserById(id, db), toPublicUser(row) (STRIPS password_hash — always serialise users through this), and types UserRow / PublicUser. UnauthorizedError is exported if other modules need to throw it.

=== GIFT_POINTS BALANCE EXPOSURE (for FEAT points/redeem features) ===
gift_points lives on the users table (INTEGER, default 0) and is returned TWO ways, both under /api/auth:
  1) GET /api/auth/me -> { user: { id, email, name, gift_points, created_at } }  (gift_points folded into the user object — the frontend auth context should read it from here on login/refresh).
  2) GET /api/auth/points -> { gift_points: number }  (lightweight balance-only endpoint for refreshing the number without re-fetching the whole user).
Recommendation for the frontend: use /api/auth/me on login/boot and after an order (points earned/redeemed changes the balance); /api/auth/points is available for a cheap refresh. Register seeds gift_points=0 and also provisions the user's cart row (INSERT INTO carts) so FEAT-004 cart ops have a home.
